base_framework_contribution: A 'local-first AI application' base framework spanning: (1) the provider-agnostic capability-compute seam + trust-tiered privacy gate + self-registering backend registry + host-adaptive detector; (2) the safe embedded-DB evolution kit (idempotent backup-first additive migrations, provenance columns, multi-user-via-nullable-owner); (3) the offline-crypto open-core licensing kit (Ed25519 verify + self-gating MoR webhook issuer, fail-safe-to-free); (4) the two-stage hybrid retrieval + dual-store ANN + graceful-degradation pattern; (5) the compose-able trust-gate pattern (parity + self-retrieval) for untrusted/remote compute; (6) the numpy-only personalization ladder over stored embeddings; (7) the vanilla-extract typed token-contract design floor. These are vertical-agnostic and seed any privacy-sensitive, embeddings-backed desktop/self-hosted app.
vertical_variation: On top of that base, tessera is the MEDIA / digital-asset-manager vertical template: a multi-tier on-device enrichment pipeline (structured tags JoyTag+WD-EVA02 / SigLIP embeddings / VLM captions / NudeNet regions), image+video catalog schema (scenes, sprites, VTT scrub, contact sheets), faces (detect+cluster), places+events (geo clustering), caption FTS, the vec_owner image+scene vector unification, and a dense keyboard-first 'Pigment' DAM UI (justified virtualized grid, facet rail with disjunctive counts, inspector, command palette, docked lightbox, Tauri desktop + Docker self-host). Swappable analogues: replace the media taggers/embedders with domain models to seed parallel verticals — a document/legal DAM, a medical-image library, a research-corpus browser — reusing the same seam, gates, licensing, migrations, and design floor.
defensibility: Low on any single component (every model is third-party/open, AGPL exposes the code, the algorithms are textbook) — but meaningfully high on the INTEGRATED DISCIPLINE that is genuinely hard to reproduce: a privacy boundary enforced as an architectural seam rather than a policy, the compose-able trust gates with honest 'this proves X not Y' reasoning that catch silent semantic failures, full provenance + safe end-user DB evolution, fail-safe-to-free offline licensing that can't be broken by going offline, and a pro-tool design floor with explicit anti-AI-slop references. The moat is the assembled correctness/privacy/taste system and the captured vendor-trap knowledge, plus open-core trust (AGPL + 'no media or core capability ever gated' + no telemetry) as a brand wedge against cloud photo apps. A competitor can re-implement any one piece in a weekend; reproducing the whole verified, privacy-first, monetizable assembly is the real cost — and that is exactly the reusable base a clean rebuild should preserve.

core_strategy: A compliance-grade "artifact of record" engine: every regulated document (a certified-payroll report) is produced by a deterministic, framework-free pure-function core that turns one normalized input contract into byte-stable output, gated by a flag-never-guess validation pass, then frozen by a single atomic LOCK transition that simultaneously (a) writes an append-only immutable version row whose immutability is a MISSING database GRANT (not a trigger), (b) snapshots a Zod-validated provenance JSONB the signer can defend under penalty of perjury, (c) writes the bytes to WORM Object-Lock storage with a per-jurisdiction retention, and (d) emits the billing meter — so immutability, provenance, retention, and billing all key off one unambiguous event. The whole thing sits on a uniform fail-closed multi-tenant RLS floor and an integer-only branded-units domain (no floats anywhere). A clean rebuild MUST preserve: lock = the one event that couples immutability+provenance+WORM+meter; output determinism enforced by a golden-file harness; and "flag, never guess" — the engine refuses to produce a record rather than fabricate a value.

reusable_principles.principle: Append-only immutability by missing privilege, not by trigger
reusable_principles.what: The versions table holds only locked rows; the app DB role has no UPDATE/DELETE grant. Current version is DERIVED (the row no other row supersedes via a supersedes_id chain), never stored as a mutable flag. Amendments are INSERT version_no+1, never UPDATE. Nothing is ever destroyed.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: A trigger can be dropped or disabled; an absent privilege cannot. For perjury-grade / audit records, immutability must be structurally impossible to violate, not policy-enforced. It also makes the billing meter and the immutability event the same INSERT.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Two roles: a constrained app role with only SELECT/INSERT on the record table, and a separate migration/admin role. Put the GRANT (and the deliberate absence of UPDATE/DELETE) in a hand-authored, reviewed migration block. Model 'current' as a NOT-IN-superseded derivation with a partial index on supersedes_id; never add updated_at to the record table (its presence implies a mutation path).

reusable_principles.principle: Uniform, fail-closed, single-template row-level tenant isolation
reusable_principles.what: One RLS policy template applied identically to every tenant table: workspace_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid, with FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and withCheck mirroring using. A denormalized workspace_id column on every table is what the policy keys on (not an FK join). A second RESTRICTIVE SELECT-only policy narrows agency-staff visibility to a JSONB company_scope.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: One template means the security auditor verifies ONE policy shape, not N hand-written predicates. The NULLIF guard defeats the silent pooled-connection footgun where a committed SET LOCAL reverts the GUC to empty-string (''::uuid raises rather than denies). Missing tenant scope yields zero rows, never all rows.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Express the policy as a single reusable factory the schema layer stamps on each table. Require a denormalized tenant-id column everywhere (a shared column helper). FORCE RLS on every table and add a CI/schema test that fails if any RLS-enabled table is not also FORCEd. Always set a validated tenant GUC at the connection seam (withWorkspace) and never trust middleware as the only gate.

reusable_principles.principle: Integer-only branded units domain with a single recorded rounding point
reusable_principles.what: Money=cents, hours=milli-hours, rates=cents-per-hour, all as compile-time branded integer types that are non-interchangeable without an explicit constructor. The only non-integer appears inside one documented intermediate, collapsed to integer at a single rounding point that emits a RoundingRecord (inputs, unrounded value, mode, result).
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: Floats silently corrupt regulated arithmetic; branding stops a milli-hours value being passed where cents are expected. The recorded rounding trail lets a portal cent-dispute be reconstructed exactly — the arithmetic IS the defense.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Define Brand<T,'X'> types and constructors that assert Number.isSafeInteger. Choose the minor unit to ingest the source's max precision losslessly (here milli-hours for a third-decimal payroll API). Centralize the one rounding function; have it RETURN a provenance record, not just a number, and snapshot those records into the locked artifact.

reusable_principles.principle: Provenance snapshot as Zod-strict-validated JSONB, parsed before INSERT
reusable_principles.what: Hybrid table: the query-hot spine (version_no, checksum, locked_at, billing_status, retain_until) is typed columns; the audit-read provenance (source+hash, mapping template, pinned determination version, full edit log, rounding records, resolved flag reasons, config version) is ONE z.strictObject JSONB. provenanceSchema.parse() runs before the INSERT.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: A JSONB column cannot self-enforce a shape; parsing at write is the required-at-write guarantee, and .strict() makes a drifted writer fail loudly instead of silently storing a malformed defense file. Typed spine keeps the meter/version queries cheap.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Split each record into 'structural columns you query' vs 'one validated evidence blob you only read in an audit.' Validate the blob with a strict schema at the write boundary, never .passthrough(). Version the blob's schema and store the schema/config version inside it so any artifact is reconstructable.

reusable_principles.principle: Field-level envelope encryption with a key-version column as the abstraction boundary
reusable_principles.what: PII (SSN) is encrypted in the APP layer (not pgcrypto, so the key never transits SQL) via a Drizzle customType doing AES-256-GCM, storing one self-describing bytea (iv‖tag‖ciphertext). A key_version column distinguishes env-key (v0) from KMS-wrapped DEK (v1); the KMS DEK is unwrapped once at boot and cached so the sync codecs stay sync. Only last-4 persists as plaintext; no blind index on the secret (keyspace too small); errors never carry plaintext.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: The key-version column makes the env-key→KMS swap a re-wrap with ZERO schema change, and makes rotation target exactly the rows that need it. Self-describing ciphertext needs no sibling columns to decrypt. This is the difference between 'SOC2 = paperwork' and 'SOC2 = re-architecture.'
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Wrap encryption in the ORM's custom column type so call sites just read/write plaintext. Pack iv+tag+ciphertext into one column. Add a key_version column from migration one even if you only ship the env key. Unwrap the DEK once at boot via KMS Decrypt and cache it; never call KMS per row. Provide a write-helper that co-stamps key_version so a bare write can't ride a default and mis-target rotation.

reusable_principles.principle: WORM artifact storage as a seam, enforced belt-and-braces
reusable_principles.what: An ArtifactStore interface with a local dev impl and an S3 Object-Lock prod impl. Write-once via conditional PUT (IfNoneMatch:'*' → ArtifactExistsError), PLUS Object-Lock retention = now + per-state retentionYears, with the EXACT retain-until also persisted on the DB row so the legal window is queryable without hitting S3. Bytes are byte-stable (sha256 is the checksum invariant); the highest-sensitivity class adds SSE-KMS under a per-tenant key.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: Two independent immutability mechanisms (conditional write + object lock) mean a single misconfig doesn't lose the WORM guarantee. The seam lets the same lock path run hermetically against minio in tests/audits, proving real Object-Lock behavior without prod writes.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Define the store as an interface first; implement local before cloud. Enforce write-once at the protocol level (conditional create), not app logic. Derive retention from the per-jurisdiction config, persist it on the row AND the object, and validate retentionYears>=floor at construction so you never silently under-retain. Keep retention metadata OUT of the artifact bytes so the checksum stays stable.

reusable_principles.principle: Config-as-code module registry gated by a golden-file determinism harness
reusable_principles.what: Each jurisdiction is a versioned, Zod-validated TypeScript config object in-repo (formats, schema versions with coexisting emitters/validators, retention, cadence, portal mechanics, rate source). The DB stores only WHICH config version each record used. A golden-file harness (fixture = input paired with byte-stable expected output) is built BEFORE any module and reruns the full matrix on every schema/form/refactor change.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: In-repo config makes 'a config change must rerun the regression matrix' structural: config change = commit = CI gate = reviewed diff. DB-resident hot-editable config is exactly the untested bypass. Determinism turns a regulatory form revision into a config swap, not a fire drill — the maintenance moat enabler for a solo operator.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Make modules pure data validated by one strict schema with a refine() for invariants (e.g. exactly one current version). Build the golden harness FIRST: discover fixtures by manifest, fail-closed per fixture (one bad fixture names itself, never aborts the matrix), support a guarded BLESS env-flag to regenerate, and a 'goldenPending' skip for forms not yet authority-verified. CI asserts every result passes.

reusable_principles.principle: Flag-never-guess: a pure two-tier validation engine that refuses rather than fabricates
reusable_principles.what: One deterministic engine is the ONLY place issues are minted; generation is disabled while ANY issue is open. Tier-1 (structural) = hard block, only fixing data clears it. Tier-2 (substantive) = blocks but clearable by an explicit recorded per-cell reason that lands in the provenance ledger. Nothing is auto-filled or auto-cleared; statements are plain-English (and double as the help/SEO corpus).
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: For a record signed under penalty of perjury, a silent auto-fill is a liability, not a convenience. Centralizing minting gives one source of truth for severity classification; recording the clearing reason into provenance makes every override defensible.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Keep the engine pure: inputs + a resolutions map in, flags + canGenerate out — clearing is applied by passing resolutions, never by mutation. Maintain one code→tier map other consumers derive from. Make Tier-1 structurally unable to carry a resolution. Persist resolutions {reason, by, at, cell} into the immutable record at lock.

reusable_principles.principle: One canonical normalized input contract with multiple idempotent producers; corrections are new versions
reusable_principles.what: A frozen DraftPayload contract is emitted by BOTH the CSV importer and the live-API (Finch) mapper, so everything downstream is producer-agnostic. Re-imports are byte-identical overwrites of the free, regenerable draft. A live-source change becomes a NEW amended version through a pure drift comparison (gross + line-count vs the locked provenance) with a tuned benign threshold → a one-click amendment prefill the user must lock — never an auto-mutation.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: Decoupling ingestion from assembly lets you add sources without touching the engine. Drift-as-signal (threshold suppresses rounding jitter) is the 'we tell you when your filing went stale' differentiator, and routing corrections through append-only versions preserves the audit chain.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Define the normalized contract as the integration point and write every ingestion adapter to emit exactly it; share the same flag engine for both. Make ingestion pure/deterministic so a re-pull is a no-op on unchanged data. For drift, compare against what the locked record actually stored (not a re-derivation), make the threshold a parameter, and require explicit user intent to create the amendment.

reusable_principles.principle: DB-anchored idempotency via partial unique indexes for billing/webhook/quota races
reusable_principles.what: Concurrency-sensitive once-only rules are anchored at the DB with partial unique indexes: meter-once-per-report (WHERE kind='meter_emitted'), webhook-event-once per (event_id, workspace), free-allocation-once-per-workspace (WHERE status='free_clean'). The app does a read-then-INSERT and catches 23505 (in a SAVEPOINT) to convert the race-loser into a structured outcome.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: Read-check-then-write always races under retries/pooling; the DB unique index is the only real anchor. This is how you bill exactly once even when Stripe retries a webhook concurrently or two requests both pass the 'first lock' read.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: For every 'at most once' business rule, add a partial unique index expressing it, then treat the app-level check as a fast-path and the unique-violation as the authoritative branch (map 23505 → the intended block/skip). Keep each catch in its own SAVEPOINT so it doesn't poison the surrounding transaction.

reusable_principles.principle: Acceptance provability without a live portal: offline schema validation + golden bytes
reusable_principles.what: The #1 priority is that the output uploads portal-clean first try. Confidence is made agent-runnable OFFLINE: a vendored portal XSD is validated against the emitted XML via WASM libxml2 (order-sensitive xs:sequence), bracketing the byte-stable emitter. No bytes lock until both the offline validator and the golden matrix pass. The business gate is two-sided: an entry spike (a real upload validates clean) plus an exit gate (a real reviewer accepts a generated record).
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: You cannot ship a compliance tool whose output gets rejected — the whole trust promise collapses on first contact. Proving acceptance offline (and in CI) de-risks every refactor and every new jurisdiction without a human round-trip to the portal.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Vendor the authority's schema verbatim into the repo (canonical URLs rot), validate with a no-native-toolchain WASM validator so it runs in CI and agents, and resolve the asset path for both test and bundled-server contexts. Gate locking on validator AND golden both green. Track the real-world acceptance proof as an explicit launch gate, separate from the code gate.

reusable_principles.principle: Fork→ADR governance: never auto-decide, record decisions append-only
reusable_principles.what: Every open decision is a 'fork' on a live board until the operator locks it; locks become append-only ADRs (never edited, superseded by later ADRs). A strict source-of-truth hierarchy (forks board > ADRs > specs > working distillations > session artifacts) resolves conflicts. No product code before the spec it implements is locked.
reusable_principles.why_it_matters: In a regulated domain, an undocumented decision is an un-auditable one. Append-only ADRs give the same immutability discipline to the project's reasoning that the product gives to its records, and the hierarchy stops doc drift.
reusable_principles.rebuild_note: Keep a single decisions-and-forks file as the live board plus an append-only numbered ADR directory. Make 'recommendation + confidence + evidence, then wait for the human lock' the default. Reconcile every other doc to the locked decision; treat a dead pointer or a second inline definition of a term as a bug.

standout_subsystems.name: The atomic LOCK & CERTIFY transition
standout_subsystems.what: One transition that capability-gates the signer, runs the flag engine on the confirmed draft and refuses while any flag is open, generates the byte-stable artifact, checksums it, parses+snapshots the provenance JSONB, INSERTs one append-only version with its resolved billing_status and per-state retain-until, writes the bytes to WORM, asserts the stored sha256 equals the checksum, and emits the meter once-per-report.
standout_subsystems.productize_as: A reusable 'certify-and-freeze' library/transaction primitive for any system that produces records of legal record — couples immutability + provenance + WORM + metering into one event with a pluggable emitter/store/flag-engine.

standout_subsystems.what: Manifest-driven fixture discovery, byte-diff with first-differing-offset reporting, fail-closed per fixture, a guarded WF_BLESS_GOLDEN regenerate path, and a 'goldenPending' skip for authority-unverified forms — built before any module and rerun on every change.
standout_subsystems.productize_as: A drop-in 'output regression vault' for any deterministic document/file emitter (PDF, XML, CSV) — sold as the safety net that turns format/spec churn into a reviewed diff.

standout_subsystems.what: AES-256-GCM Drizzle customType storing self-describing iv‖tag‖ciphertext, KMS-DEK unwrapped once at boot, a key_version column making env→KMS a zero-schema-change re-wrap, last-4-only plaintext, no blind index, plaintext-free errors, timing-safe equality.
standout_subsystems.productize_as: A 'PII column kit' for ORMs (Drizzle/Prisma): envelope-encrypted custom types + a rotation-aware key registry + masking helpers, marketed as SOC2/HIPAA-ready field encryption you add per-column.

base_framework_contribution: A 'compliance-grade records platform' base that many reg-tech verticals can derive from. Concretely the reusable spine: (1) a uniform fail-closed multi-tenant RLS column-helper + policy factory with a connection-seam GUC and a FORCE-RLS schema test; (2) an append-only-by-grant versioning module (record table + supersedes chain + derived-current predicate + two-role grant migration); (3) a branded integer-units domain with a single-rounding-point provenance record; (4) a write-time Zod-strict provenance-JSONB pattern (typed spine + validated evidence blob); (5) a field-encryption ORM customType + key-version rotation registry + KMS envelope helper + masking; (6) a WORM ArtifactStore seam (local + S3 Object-Lock) with retention-on-row-and-object and byte-stable checksums; (7) a config-as-code module registry validated by a golden-file determinism harness with a BLESS path; (8) a pure two-tier flag/validation engine with override-with-reason recording; (9) DB-anchored idempotency via partial unique indexes + 23505 mapping; (10) a ledger-tracked hermetic audit harness; (11) fork→append-only-ADR governance with a source-of-truth hierarchy. Everything above is domain-agnostic and could ship as the shared base under multiple vertical templates.
vertical_variation: Wardfile is the certified-payroll / Davis-Bacon prevailing-wage vertical template seeded on that base: WH-347 PDF + multi-state portal emitters (CA DIR eCPR XML V1.3, IL IDOL CTP CSV, WA L&I worksheet+roster CSV, NJ MW-562), wage-determination harvest+pinning, worker→classification→WD-line mapping, the day-split step (no source emits per-day hours), fringe/annualization and OT math, apprentice ratio/registration rules, Finch payroll ingestion + universal CSV templates, an agency multi-EIN white-label workspace, and the preparer/signer 'core loop' UX. Swapping the jurisdiction config packs, emitters/validators, golden fixtures, the domain flag codes, and the ingestion adapters — while keeping the base spine intact — would reseed the same platform as a different reg-tech vertical (e.g. sales-tax filing, environmental/EPA reporting, clinical/HIPAA records, ESG disclosures).
defensibility: The moat is the bundle and the maintenance discipline, not any single feature (the team explicitly re-classified live ingestion as the WEDGE, not the moat). Durable layers: (1) Accepted+defensible output — golden-file determinism + offline vendored-XSD validation prove portal-acceptance first-try and per-state, which is expensive to replicate and must be re-earned on every regulatory form/schema revision; the byte-stability + provenance ledger only matter because append-only versioning + live ingestion exist together, so they can't be cheaply bolted on. (2) Per-state depth — CA eCPR (full-SSN decrypt-at-emit, order-sensitive XSD) is the hardest artifact in the category; each new state is multi-week regulatory research locked behind golden fixtures, a compounding per-state cost that punishes shallow entrants. (3) The flag-never-guess trust posture under penalty of perjury — a competitor that auto-fills is taking on liability, so the discipline is a positioning lock, not just a feature. (4) A compliance-grade substrate (uniform fail-closed RLS + WORM Object-Lock + KMS field encryption + append-only) where SOC2 is paperwork, not re-architecture — a late entrant must rebuild the data layer. (5) The empty agency multi-EIN lane plus distribution through bookkeepers. The vulnerability the team itself names: a platform incumbent (QBO) adding state-portal XML, or per-state regulatory churn outpacing the golden-maintenance cadence — which is precisely why the determinism harness and config-as-code gate are the load-bearing defenses.
